## How it works

- [statement] ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES selects AMD ROCm GPUs. List devices with `rocminfo`, and use the Uuid when available. An invalid ID such as -1 forces CPU. (low confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/gpu · keywords: Ollama GPU backends and hardware support: CUDA / ROCm / Vulkan / device selection env vars
- [statement] Vulkan is the documented path for GPUs that ROCm does not cover. Per the current docs it is enabled by default when the backend is installed. OLLAMA_VULKAN=0 or GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1 disables all Vulkan GPUs. GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES takes numeric IDs to select specific Vulkan GPUs. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/gpu · keywords: Ollama GPU backends and hardware support: CUDA / ROCm / Vulkan / device selection env vars · also: https://www.phoronix.com/news/ollama-0.12.11-Vulkan
- [statement] On a mixed iGPU/dGPU system where the Vulkan iGPU is unstable, keep Vulkan on and set GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES to the discrete GPU index (for example 1 when Vulkan1 is the discrete GPU). (low confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/gpu · keywords: Ollama GPU backends and hardware support: CUDA / ROCm / Vulkan / device selection env vars

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES takes a comma-separated list to limit Ollama to a subset of NVIDIA GPUs. UUIDs (from `nvidia-smi -L`) are more reliable than numeric IDs because ordering may vary. An invalid ID such as -1 forces CPU. (low confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/gpu · keywords: Ollama GPU backends and hardware support: CUDA / ROCm / Vulkan / device selection env vars
- [statement] Vulkan cannot read free VRAM unless Ollama runs as root or the binary has cap_perfmon (`sudo setcap cap_perfmon+ep /usr/local/bin/ollama`). Without either, the scheduler uses approximate model sizes. On some Linux distributions the ollama user must also join the render group for AMD GPUs. (low confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/gpu · keywords: Ollama GPU backends and hardware support: CUDA / ROCm / Vulkan / device selection env vars
- [statement] On Linux after a suspend/resume cycle, Ollama can fail to find the NVIDIA GPU and fall back to CPU. Reloading the UVM driver works around it: `sudo rmmod nvidia_uvm && sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm`. (low confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/gpu · keywords: Ollama GPU backends and hardware support: CUDA / ROCm / Vulkan / device selection env vars

## Facts and statements

- [statement] NVIDIA support needs compute capability 5.0+ and driver 550 or newer. Cards with compute capability 5.0 through 6.2 need driver 570 or newer. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/gpu · keywords: Ollama GPU backends and hardware support: CUDA / ROCm / Vulkan / device selection env vars
- [statement] On Linux, Ollama requires the AMD ROCm v7 driver. On Windows it requires a ROCm v7 / HIP7-capable driver stack. The Windows supported-card list is shorter than the Linux list (Radeon RX 7600 through 7900 XTX and Radeon PRO W7500 through W7900). (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/gpu · keywords: Ollama GPU backends and hardware support: CUDA / ROCm / Vulkan / device selection env vars
- [statement] HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=x.y.z forces ROCm to use a nearby supported LLVM target for an unsupported AMD GPU, for example 10.3.0 for a gfx1032 or gfx1034 card. With mixed GPUs, append the device number (HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION_0, HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION_1). The documented override is Linux-only. (medium confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/gpu · keywords: Ollama GPU backends and hardware support: CUDA / ROCm / Vulkan / device selection env vars · also: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/2870
- [statement] Vulkan first shipped as experimental. On 2025-11-14 Phoronix reported ollama 0.12.11 with Vulkan enabled by setting OLLAMA_VULKAN=1, aimed at older AMD GPUs without ROCm support and RADV systems without ROCm installed. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-11-14) — https://www.phoronix.com/news/ollama-0.12.11-Vulkan · keywords: Ollama GPU backends and hardware support: CUDA / ROCm / Vulkan / device selection env vars
- [statement] With SELinux, containers may be denied access to AMD GPU devices. Run `sudo setsebool container_use_devices=1` on the host. (low confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/gpu · keywords: Ollama GPU backends and hardware support: CUDA / ROCm / Vulkan / device selection env vars
- [statement] Without HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION, an unsupported gfx1032 card (RX 6650 XT) crashed in rocBLAS with a missing TensileLibrary.dat and a segmentation fault. Setting 10.3.0 in the docker run command fixed it (ollama/ollama:0.1.27-rocm, March 2024). (low confidence) — https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/2870 · keywords: Ollama GPU backends and hardware support: CUDA / ROCm / Vulkan / device selection env vars
